companies.fiscal: Financial year ends in late March. Calendar Q3 2026 is Burberry's Q2 FY27.
companies.scope: Series and regions are comparable retail sales: stores open for a year, at constant exchange rates. Retail is about 85% of revenue. Burberry reports Asia in two parts. guidance.text: Expects further progress on its financial ambitions in FY27, with revenue growth and margin expansion, while mindful of an uncertain geopolitical and macroeconomic environment.

companies.name: Brunello Cucinelli
companies.scope: Brunello Cucinelli publishes second-quarter sales only inside the half year, so the second quarters are left empty. First-half revenues grew 13.3% at constant rates in 2026 and 10.7% in 2025. Regions are published for the year to date and not for the quarter, so the region columns are empty. The fourth quarter of 2024 is left out because the company gave that figure without a constant-rate basis.
companies.china: Brunello Cucinelli reports strong growth in China and names it as a significant contributor to Asia. The company gives no growth figure for China or for Asia in the quarter.

guidance.text: Revenue growth of 12% at constant exchange rates in 2026, raised from a range of 10% to 11% in July. Around 10% in 2027.
guidance.evidence: Growth at constant rates was 13.3% in the first half and 13.5% in the third quarter.
guidance.read: Ahead of the full-year target after nine months.

companies.name: Ferragamo
companies.scope: Group growth is total revenues. The regions are net sales. Central and South America grew 0.7% in the third quarter and 6.5% in the second, and has no matching column.
companies.china: Ferragamo said the market weakened during the third quarter, with the trend in Asia deteriorating further, in particular in China. Asia Pacific net sales fell 11.1% at constant rates, after a 0.6% decline in the second quarter.

guidance.text: No numeric guidance. The group says it remains confident in its medium to long-term direction and will keep executing with discipline amid macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty.
guidance.evidence: Third-quarter revenues fell 3.5% at constant rates, after growth of 4.6% in the second quarter.

companies.name: Ferrari
companies.scope: Growth is net revenues at constant currency. Ferrari reports shipments by region, not revenue, so the region columns are empty. Releases from the fourth quarter of 2025 onward round growth to whole numbers, and so does the fourth quarter of 2024, which comes from the release's table.
companies.china: Ferrari shipped 3,368 cars in the third quarter, 33 fewer than a year earlier, and reports shipments by region rather than revenue.

guidance.text: Net revenues of about €7.65 billion in 2026, raised from about €7.60 billion. Net revenues were €7.15 billion in 2025.
guidance.evidence: Nine-month net revenues were €5,682 million, up 6%.
guidance.read: Testable at the full-year results in February.

companies.name: Aston Martin
companies.scope: Growth is total revenue as reported, in sterling: Aston Martin publishes no constant-currency figure. Valhalla deliveries, which began in the fourth quarter of 2025, make revenue swing from quarter to quarter. The company reports wholesale units by region, not revenue, so the region columns are empty. The announcements are the company's own regulatory releases (RNS), linked on the London Stock Exchange or on sites that republish RNS in full.

companies.china: Aston Martin reports wholesale volumes by region, not revenue, and gives no revenue figure for China.

guidance.text: Full-year 2026 guidance unchanged: a material improvement in financial performance on 2025.
guidance.evidence: Revenue grew 16%, 62% and 36% in the first three quarters of 2026.

peer.note: 9 of 9 companies grew more slowly in Q3 2026 than in Q2 2026. Median growth went from +5% in Q2 2026 to +1% for the 9 companies that report both quarters. In Asia excluding Japan it went from +8.3% to +2.5%. Asia grew more slowly than the group at 6 of 9 companies.
peer.lede: Median growth went from +5% in Q2 2026 to +1% for the 9 companies that report both quarters. In Asia excluding Japan it went from +8.3% to +2.5%.

lvmh.note: LVMH organic growth was 1% in Q3 2026, down from 3% in Q2 2026, a change of -2 points. Asia excl. Japan drove the slowdown, moving to -5% from 4%, a change of -9 points, with management citing a less buoyant China that hit Fashion & Leather Goods, which was -5%. Japan grew 6%, the United States 5% and Europe 4%. Growth was 3 points behind the median of the other companies in the peer_group, which was 4%.
lvmh.watch: Check whether Asia excl. Japan returns to growth and whether Fashion & Leather Goods improves from -5% in the next release.

hermes.note: Hermès growth at Constant FX was 4.3% in Q3 2026, down from 6.7% in Q2 2026, a change of -2.4 points. The two-year stack is 14.3%. The largest driver was the Americas, where the change was -4.9 points, leaving growth at 8.8%. Asia-Pacific excl. Japan was 0%, 4.3 points below the company figure. Three of five regions grew. Growth was 3.3 points above the median of the other companies in the Personal luxury goods peer_group, which was 1%.
hermes.watch: Check whether Asia-Pacific excl. Japan moves back above 0% and whether Americas growth stabilises after its -4.9 point change this quarter.

kering.note: Kering's comparable growth was -1% in Q3 2026, down from 2% in Q2 2026, a change of -3 points. Asia Pacific was -5%, and management cited lower store traffic, particularly in Mainland China. Gucci was -6%, with its own retail sales down 9%. Kering Jewelry grew 11%. Three of five regions grew. Growth was 5 points behind the median of the other companies in the Personal luxury goods peer_group, which was 4%.
kering.watch: Check whether Asia Pacific and Gucci retail sales improve against a tougher base, with the year-earlier group growth to lap at -3%.

richemont.note: Richemont's Q3 2026 growth was 13% at Constant FX, down from 20% in Q2 2026, a change of -7 points. The two-year stack was 28.8%. Japan was the main driver, with its growth change of -13 points. Asia Pacific grew 10%, 11 points slower than the prior quarter and 3 points below the group. Four of five regions grew. Growth was 12 points above the median of the other companies in the Personal luxury goods peer_group, at 1%.
richemont.watch: Check whether Asia Pacific growth stabilises and whether Middle East & Africa returns to growth, given the group laps 11% growth next quarter.

moncler.note: Moncler's Q3 2026 growth at Constant FX was 0%, down from 5% in Q2 2026, a slowdown of 5 points. Asia was the main driver, growing 5% after a 7 point slower pace than the prior quarter. EMEA fell 8% and Americas grew 2%. Two of three regions grew. Growth was 4 points behind the median of the other companies in the Personal luxury goods peer_group, at 4%.
moncler.watch: Check whether Asia growth recovers from 5% and whether EMEA improves from -8%, given the group growth to lap next quarter is 7%.

prada.note: Prada Group organic retail growth was 0% in Q3 2026, down from 5% in Q2 2026, a fall of 5 points. The driver was the Americas, where growth slowed by 14 points to 5%. Asia Pacific was 0%, 8 points lower than the prior quarter. Europe was -3% and the Middle East was -18%. Only 1 of 5 regions grew. Growth was 4 points behind the median of the other companies in the peer_group, which was 4%.
prada.watch: Check whether more than 1 of the 5 regions grows in Q4 2026 and how Asia Pacific and the Americas move against the 5.6% base being lapped.

burberry.note: Burberry's comparable growth was 4% in Q3 2026, down from 5% in Q2 2026, a change of -1 point. Greater China was the main driver: it grew 5% after 9% in the prior quarter, a slowdown of 4 points. Americas grew 11% and EMEIA was -2%. Growth was 3 points ahead of the median of the other companies in the peer_group, which was 1%. Two of three regions grew.
burberry.watch: Check whether Greater China comparable retail sales growth steadies or slows again from 5%, and whether EMEIA returns to growth from -2%.

zegna.note: Zegna Group's organic growth was 8.2% in Q3 2026, down from 11.0% in Q2 2026, a slowdown of 2.8 points. The Americas was the main driver of the change, with a change of -8.2 points on the model's driver line, though it still grew 13.6%. The Greater China Region grew 5.7%, after 8.6% in the second quarter. Thom Browne fell 7.4%. Growth was 7.2 points above the median of the other companies in the peer_group, which was 1%.
zegna.watch: Check whether the Americas growth rate and the Greater China Region growth rate move further from the Q3 2026 levels of 13.6% and 5.7%, and whether Thom Browne returns to growth.

cucinelli.note: Brunello Cucinelli grew 13.5% at constant FX in Q3 2026, but there is no prior quarter figure to compare with, because Q2 sales are published only inside the half year. The two-year stack was 27.7%. Growth was 12.5 points ahead of the median of the other companies in the peer_group, which was 1%. Management cites strong growth in China but gives no figure for China or Asia.
cucinelli.watch: Check whether the company publishes a regional or China growth figure for the quarter and how growth compares with the 11.9% to be lapped.

ferragamo.note: Ferragamo's Q3 2026 growth at Constant FX was -3.5%, down from 4.6% in Q2 2026, a change of -8.1 points. Asia Pacific fell 11.1% after a 0.6% decline in Q2, and management said the trend in Asia worsened, in particular in China. Only 1 of 4 regions grew: North America at 2.4%. Japan was -5.0% and EMEA was -5.2%. The gap to the median of the other companies in the Personal luxury goods peer_group (4%) was -7.5 points.
ferragamo.watch: Check whether Asia Pacific and China stop deteriorating in the next release and whether more than one region grows, given the group growth to lap of -2.0%.

ferrari.note: Ferrari's Q3 2026 growth was 10% at Constant FX, down from 11% in Q2 2026, a change of -1 point. Cars and spare parts grew 10%, Sponsorship, commercial and brand grew 7%, and Other grew 17%. The two-year stack is 20.2%. Growth a year earlier was 9.3%, and the base to lap next quarter is 6%. Shipments were 3,368 cars, 33 fewer than a year earlier. No regional revenue is reported.
ferrari.watch: Check whether growth in cars and spare parts holds against the easier base of 6% and whether the net revenues guidance of about €7.65 billion is changed again.

aston-martin.note: Aston Martin's reported revenue growth was 36% in Q3 2026, against 62% in Q2 2026, a slowdown of 26 points. The data does not attribute the change to a region or segment, because the company reports wholesale units by region, not revenue. Valhalla deliveries make revenue swing from quarter to quarter. Group growth a year earlier was -27%, and the base to lap next quarter is -12%. Full-year guidance is unchanged.
aston-martin.watch: Check whether reported revenue growth in the next release holds against the tougher base of -12% and whether Valhalla deliveries continue to drive the quarterly swings.

taxonomy.note: How companies and their segments are grouped. industries are peer groups: each company is compared only with the others in its own industry, and every median is taken within one. focus splits an industry by what the company mostly sells. categories group segments across companies, so leather goods can be read against leather goods. A median is shown only for a group of at least min_group members, and never for a category marked no_median, whose lines have nothing in common. In segments, a name mapped to null is a line inside another one, such as Gucci inside Kering's fashion line, and is left out of the category so nothing is counted twice.
